script: Giant manta rays can measure about 7 meters from wingtip to wingtip. They are the largest rays in the ocean. For their body size, mantas have one of the biggest brains of any fish. Despite their size, they feed on tiny plankton filtered from the water. Each manta has a unique pattern of spots on its belly. Scientists use those patterns to recognize individual mantas, like fingerprints. Follow Pixel Abyss for more strange facts from the deep.
